summary: No Credo release or filing beyond an insider Form 4 on Nov 23. Stifel trimmed its price target on Nov 24, and optical rival Applied Optoelectronics signed a $2.2B 800G transceiver supply deal with an unnamed hyperscaler, which sits inside the optical market the research already sizes. The stock fell about 13% with the chip giveback; the Dec 1 print stays the deciding event.

items.headline: Applied Optoelectronics signs $2.2B multi-year 800G transceiver and laser supply deal with a Tier-1 hyperscaler
items.why: Company release (PRNewswire relay): ~$1.5B 800G transceivers in 2027, ~$0.7B laser diodes 2028-29, customer unnamed, DSP vendor not stated. It is hyperscaler optical demand inside the LightCounting-based optical TAM; it shows a rival transceiver vendor locking volume, but with no named customer or DSP vendor it cannot be mapped to Credo's optical share. No driver move.

items.headline: Credo down 13.1% as AI chip stocks give back Monday's surge
items.why: Sector price move only; no customer, competitor-share or capex fact. A price move alone is never a trigger.
